text:
Maya: FYI — I found inconsistent examples for the /users/{id} endpoint. Some request examples show numeric ids (12345) but responses and SDK snippets show canonical string ids like 'u_12345'. This is confusing people in migration notes. Anyone on this?

Chris: Ah, I noticed that too in the OpenAPI. Do we have a canonical format? Backend accepts both, right?

Maya: @Chris backend team confirmed the canonical form is a string with a 'u_' prefix. They still accept bare numbers for legacy clients but responses always return the canonical string. We should standardize docs to show the canonical id in the main examples and include a small legacy example and migration note.

Jordan: I can take this. Plan: update OpenAPI example values to use `u_12345` as the primary example, keep a secondary example showing `12345` with a note. Also update the python/go SDK snippets so examples expect string ids. Add a tiny migration code snippet for users migrating from numeric ids.

Maya: SGTM. Also add an explicit sentence in the API reference like: "id may be provided as legacy numeric or canonical string; responses are always canonical string prefixed with 'u_'." 

Chris: For SDK examples, watch out — some generated Go examples currently show `ID int64` in example structs. That will confuse readers. We should make the examples show `ID string` and include a short deserialization note for legacy payloads.

Jordan: Good catch. I won't change the server schema (it can remain `oneOf: [integer, string]`) — just change the examples and the snippets. I'll include a short Go snippet that normalizes incoming numeric ids to the canonical string before use.

Jordan: ```python
# normalize numeric legacy id to canonical string id
raw = user_response['id']
if isinstance(raw, int):
    user_id = f"u_{raw}"
else:
    user_id = str(raw) if str(raw).startswith('u_') else f"u_{raw}"
# call client with canonical id
client.get_user(user_id)
```

Maya: :thumbsup: Please also add a short note in the migration guide and create a redirect from the old example link if possible.

docs-bot: Created issue #1847 and draft PR #2792 with the OpenAPI example updates: https://git.redwood/g/infra/docs/pulls/2792

Chris: I'll review PR #2792 later today. Jordan, ping me when it's ready for review. Also can we add a small docs-e2e test that asserts examples show the canonical form (regex `^u_\d+`)?

Jordan: Will do — adding tests + go/python snippet changes. ETA: EOD today.

Maya: Thanks everyone. After the PR merges I'll add a short note in the docs release notes. We won't change SDK types now, just examples and migration guidance, so no breaking-change entry needed unless we decide to change generated types later.
